verbalization: Prednisolone, a corticosteroid, is implicated in the pathogenesis of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) through its anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. The visible evidence suggests a potential reutilization of Prednisolone for RA, as it is linked to Discoid Lupus Erythematosus (DLE), a condition with a known association with RA. The indirect pathway through Chloroquine, which is used in the treatment of DLE, further supports this relationship. While the direct mechanism linking Prednisolone to RA remains unclear, the observed indications and the shared pathophysiological features between DLE and RA imply a possible role of Prednisolone in modulating immune responses. The integration of these pathways suggests that Prednisolone may exert a therapeutic effect on RA through mechanisms involving immune modulation, though further mechanistic studies are required to confirm this.
